{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 supports comparisons of success on unfamiliar grid problems under specified evaluation conditions. Example-based tasks, checks for repeated rules and selection informed by human solving provide reasons to connect its content to rule inference. They do not establish that scores uniquely measure reasoning or broader intelligence. Scoring is explicit: each input requires an exact match within two attempts, and input success fractions are averaged within problems before averaging across problems. Consequently, the reported score differs from the proportion of problems fully solved and does not describe partial correctness within a grid. Verified settings and spending limits help make comparisons interpretable, but public exposure, differing testing routes and revisions require attention to the conditions and version behind each result. Human difficulty matching supports the construction of the three sets; it does not establish equivalent AI difficulty or stable AI scores. Single-run verification and absent repeatability estimates limit confidence in small differences. Public materials support inspection, while incomplete verification of archives and marking software leaves some reporting and implementation questions unresolved.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The tasks directly test producing grid outputs from example pairs, supporting claims about performance on this form of rule inference.",
        "Human solving informed selection and difficulty matching, although the study pool exceeded the final test sets.",
        "The inspected software awards fractional problem credit across inputs, with exact matching required for each input.",
        "Recorded settings, spending limits and dated corrections support interpretation of verified results when the applicable conditions and version are identified."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "The change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples; affected AI scores are not all recalculated.",
        "Verified evaluations use one run, leaving reported results without an average across repeated runs.",
        "Public evaluation problems are accessible, and the hidden-test safeguards acknowledge possible information escape.",
        "Software scores can be mistaken for fully solved problem rates because the published instructions use a stricter meaning of a solved problem."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Repeated identical-test results and systematic studies of changes to instructions, grid presentation or software are absent.",
        "The supplied studies do not show prediction of performance in language, social interaction or real-world work.",
        "The reviewed evidence does not establish that all unintended routes to high scores have been excluded.",
        "The complete results archive and whole marking system were not independently checked in this survey."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Read a score as averaged exact-input success under the stated attempt allowance, rather than a count of fully solved puzzles.",
        "Treat similar human difficulty across sets as construction evidence, rather than evidence of interchangeable AI scores.",
        "Interpret a high score as grid-task performance consistent with rule inference; broader intelligence claims remain unresolved.",
        "Compare systems with attention to exposure, settings, spending, testing route and revisions, since these conditions may differ."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Reporting should clarify whether “solved” means exact input success or complete problem success, and identify the test version and evaluation conditions. The passage gives no operational boundary for what counts as changing a system specifically for evaluation problems."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA provides a practical, bounded assessment of finding and applying Formula SAE rules and interpreting selected vehicle materials. Real rules, designs and practitioner contributions support the relevance of its questions to those activities. Coverage remains narrow, and the uneven groups provide very different amounts of evidence: 1,192 individual-rule questions contrast with 16 performance questions. Equal weighting prevents question counts alone from determining the overall score, but combines different marking methods without evidence that the result measures a distinct underlying skill. Documented sensitivity to wording and omitted valid answers complicates interpretation of scores as understanding. Comparisons also depend on information supply because systems receive either the whole rulebook or retrieved passages. Reported variations in supplied materials reveal sensitivity to conditions but do not establish repeatability under identical conditions. Public materials permit partial inspection, while incomplete historical records constrain reproduction. Scores therefore describe performance on these tasks with particular inputs and scoring rules; they offer limited support for close rankings or general engineering competence.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The six groups cover rule retrieval, terminology, component identification, dimensions and performance checks using real competition materials.",
        "Additional reviewers checked manually written questions, subject to stated exceptions and more limited checks of some explanations.",
        "The authors examined changes in passages and visual presentation, providing evidence about sensitivity to supplied information.",
        "Public questions, instructions, scoring code and some responses allow inspection of parts of the evaluation."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Wording and formatting affect credit, including missing commas and valid related rules omitted from reference answers.",
        "Systems receive different information supplies, so comparisons reflect both the AI and its access to relevant material.",
        "All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes response to receive decision credit on that portion; actual use of this strategy is not established.",
        "One released answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count, and historical inputs, settings and software are not fully linked to results.",
        "The 16-question performance group is coarse: one additional correct answer changes accuracy by 6.25 percentage points."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Reviewer disagreement, remaining answer errors and comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency are not established.",
        "Identical-condition repeatability evidence and sufficient information to assess small differences in the main comparisons are absent.",
        "No human-engineer baseline, protected test set or systematic overlap check was established in the reviewed sources.",
        "Clear training and repeated-submission rules, a licence file and a score-impact change record were not found.",
        "Performance on other technical documents and prediction of success in engineering projects remain unestablished."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Interpret results as performance of an AI with its information supply, rather than attributing every difference to the model.",
        "Treat the overall score as an equal-weight summary of six groups, rather than an established measure of engineering understanding.",
        "Read text-similarity credit with the documented wording and reference-answer limitations in mind.",
        "Use real-material relevance to support task-specific interpretation, while leaving transfer to other standards and projects unresolved.",
        "Treat unavailable reuse documentation as a gap in the inspected materials, rather than evidence that reuse is prohibited."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Reports should make information supply, scoring and historical versions explicit. The inspected sources leave training and repeated-submission instructions unclear; reuse permission is also unresolved by the missing documentation."
    }
  ]
}
